neet_che_u20_t04_1.working: Weak acid vs strong base gives an equivalence point near pH 8-9. The pH jump lies in the basic range, so phenolphthalein (pH 8.2-10) is suitable.

neet_che_u20_t04_2.working: 1.26/126 = 0.01 mol in 250 mL, so 0.04 M. 25 mL holds 0.001 mol of the diprotic acid, needing 0.002 mol NaOH. 0.002/0.020 L = 0.10 M.

neet_che_u20_t04_3.working: Weak base vs strong acid has its pH jump in the acidic range, so methyl orange is used. It is yellow in the basic flask and turns red at the end point.

neet_che_u20_t04_4.working: A is true: only a few drops are added so the indicator does not noticeably affect the titration. R is false: indicators are weak organic acids or bases and do react (they are themselves titrated).

neet_che_u20_t04_5.working: I is correct: the strong acid-strong base jump is about pH 3-11, so both indicators work. II is correct: the strong acid-weak base jump is acidic (about pH 3-7), so methyl orange works.
